title: DeLiBA-K: Speeding-up Hardware-Accelerated Distributed Storage Access by Tighter Linux Kernel Integration and Use of a Modern API
problem: User-space interactions in DeLiBA-1 and -2 introduce overhead when accessing hardware-accelerated distributed storage. DeLiBA-K addresses this by operating at the Linux kernel level to reduce latency and improve I/O parallelism.
motivation: Efficient hardware-accelerated I/O is critical for improving performance in data-intensive enterprise applications and large-scale distributed systems.
method: DeLiBA-K operates at the Linux kernel level, directly interacting with the block and network I/O kernel stack rather than through user-space. It implements the modern io_uring Asynchronous I/O (AIO) API within a 16nm AMD Alveo U280 FPGA I/O framework. This kernel-level integration with io_uring enables better parallelism and reduced latency by eliminating user-space context switching overhead.
key_novelty: Kernel-level integration of io_uring asynchronous I/O API with FPGA-accelerated distributed storage access to eliminate user-space overhead.
contributions: Kernel-level reimplementation of DeLiBA framework bypassing user-space interactions
Integration of io_uring Asynchronous I/O API with AMD Alveo U280 FPGA framework
